The question numbers below are a SNAPSHOT OF AN UNFINISHED RUN. Generation
was still going when this was written; see REVIEW.md.
profileFoldDigest: see validate-pack output; changing it invalidates the built index

_note: Parsed from the Perseus TEI of Smyth, all four parts, §§ 1-3048 with no
gaps. The 266 not-teachable are Part I (letters, sounds, accent, §§ 1-188)
and Part III (word formation, §§ 822-899); the appendix's catalogue of
verbs carries no section numbers and is not a source section at all.
Runs over 12000 chars are cut at a section boundary, which is why the max
sits well under maxTextChars. 22 topics still exceed 4x the median; all
are syntax chapters and all are inside the gate.
INCOMPLETE. Generation is a resumable run that had covered 3 of 485
topics when this was committed, so gates C1, C5 and C7 fail — a topic
with no questions is what C1 exists to report. Measured rate was about
2.1 tests a minute.
Validation kept 100% of generated items over the first three topics,
which is the number to watch: Latin needed its function-word list
extended twice before it got there, and Greek needed no such list at all
because the reference dictionary is built from a morphological analyser
rather than a dump of inflected forms.
Both reference databases were built for this pack from Eulexis (GPLv3,
Morpheus-derived) and a corpus of 46 works, ~900k words of Attic prose
plus Homer and Herodotus, using scripts/reference/. At 257 MB the
dictionary is not committed and is not needed: what ships is the derived
table and the distilled frequency list, which is what the gates read.
Rebuilt on 2026-08-06 to ship the whole dictionary rather than only the
lemmas a corpus ranks — the same change Latin got, and for the same
reason: a word the corpus never used came back unknown however plainly
the reference held it. distinctLemmas 24,322 -> 97,028, formKeys
refLemmaEntries equals refEntries here, and that is the interesting
difference from Latin. Eulexis is a headword dictionary with a separate
forms table, so it has no wordform entries to exclude; Latin's kaikki
dump is 94% wordform entries. The same skip rule runs over both and
simply finds nothing to skip in this one.
formKeys fell relative to the ranked-only build in one respect worth
noting: the rebuild is a fresh join plus --merge, and --drop-artifacts
still keeps Morpheus double-compound notation (`ἐπί-εἴδομαι`) out of
both halves.
meanGlossChars is 14 across the whole table because Eulexis gives every
entry exactly one short sense. There is no sense cap to raise and no
tail-versus-ranked gloss split to make: unlike Latin, the tail costs the
same per word as the band does.
packResolvedPct is unchanged at 99.5. `attests` asks for a ranked record
now rather than merely a key, so the gates are exactly as strict as they
were when the table held ranked lemmas alone.
paradigmTagSignatures is 9,466 against Latin's 417, because Morpheus
tags nearly every form with the dialects it belongs to. That is also why
profile.paradigms declares a primary and secondary tag list where Latin
declares none: without it a genitive singular offers five spellings.
1,166 -> 1,108: 24 elided function words and 34 mid-sentence proper
nouns the checker now exempts as the generator always did. ἐφ’ is on the
allowlist, but the validator stripped only the ASCII apostrophe while the
tokenizer that reads a shipped answer strips both, so the list could
never see what it was written for.
Latin's repair does not port. Wiktionary marks a wordform entry with the
lemma it is a form of; this dictionary is analyser-built and carries no
such link on any of 60,000 entries sampled, and rebuilding at the full
frequency list changes attestation by exactly nothing — 0 tokens gained,
0 lost. The map was already built that way.
What is left is real Greek the analyser does not enumerate: future and
aorist optatives (ζημιωθήσοιτο, νοστήσοι, στήσειαν), προ- compounds of
δίδωμι and ἔρχομαι whose parent lemma is ranked (προδίδωμι is 919) but
whose augmented forms are absent, and duals. The topics they sit in are
sm-2617 and sm-2710 on indirect discourse and sm-2677 on moods in
indirect questions — which is to say the forms are there because the
grammar point is. 1,108 is a budget, not a defect list: it has no
headroom, so a later run that teaches another mood the analyser does not
enumerate raises it deliberately and says which questions bought it.
320 further tokens are in reference/dictionary.db and not shipped. Their
cause is separate and unfixed: Morpheus writes a compound headword as
κατά-κάθημαι, which does not join the frequency list's κάθημαι, so every
compound verb's forms ship rankless. ἐκάθηντο ×21 is the largest.
Only grammar and tests are precached. The three dictionary files are
fetched on demand, and the paradigms only when a word is asked for its
own table.
The dictionary went from 2.3 MB to 5.0 MB across its two files when the
tail went in. The precached half is unchanged in kind, and the screens
that warn about the download now measure it at build time rather than
naming a figure typed by hand (see __DICTIONARY_BYTES__).
